cr_data.provenance: Artist; to Alfred Stieglitz (her husband); to Artist (his wife); to Fisk University, Nashville, TN, 1949; to Fisk University, Nashville, TN, and Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art, Bentonville, AR, as co-owners, 2012 (Source: Crystal Bridges, 2025)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Infor. from Miss Bry (An Amer. Place), July 1949: On permanent loan to Fisk University, Nashville, Tennessee, from Georgia O'Keeffe as part of the Alfred Stieglitz Coll." Inscription 8 dates 1925. Inscription 10, Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks date 1927. Dated 1927 on basis of inclusion in 1928 New York (Intimate Gallery– O'Keeffe) exhibition. Titled *Radiator Building – Night /New York* by Stieglitz on Abiquiú Notebooks photograph; reproduced in *Art in America* (1929); reproduced and titled *The American Radiator Building at Night* in *New York Herald-Tribune* (December 1929); reproduced in *Outlook and Independent* (January 1930); reproduced as *New York's Black Tower* in *Fortune* (April 1935); reproduced in *Newsweek* (July 1944); titled *Radiator Building* in *The Philadelphia Museum Bulletin* (June 1945). See cat. no. 1894. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: A tall, black skyscraper rises dramatically into the night sky. Light shines from some of the windows in the building and other structures around it, creating a patchwork of black and white. At the top of one of the buildings, text rendered in red neon reads Alfred Stieglitz. Steam or smoke spreads across the deep blue sky, which is illuminated by the beams of unseen searchlights.
